scope: All timings use native 8x8 cells, original scene VBO and CUDA poses. No subrays, high-resolution rendering, mesh simplification or production changes.

static_analysis.invariant: Every positive-area triangle/cell-cone overlap participates; choose nearest Euclidean hit and its ID.
front_end: All scene triangles are transformed and processed once for every pose; there is no range/spatial broad phase.
Each GS invocation FP64-clips a triangle against five view planes before its projected cell bounding box.
The cell rectangle expands one cell on every side; a triangle contained in one interior cell can generate nine cell fragments.
fragment: Every candidate triangle/cell pair repeats five-plane FP64 clipping, projected-area filtering and exact nearest-point work.
Local fixed arrays and variable loops may produce register pressure or spills; timing alone cannot establish actual spills.
Depth is explicitly written only after nearest-radius calculation; regular early-Z rejection must not be assumed.
FP64 cost is a hypothesis; compare isolated GS/FS precision ablations before assigning causality.
safe_direction: Use convex half-space trivial accept/reject before full clipping, keeping the current partial clip algorithm.
A conservative triangle/object/BVH broad phase can reject triangles outside the cell cone or max-range sphere without approximating surviving intersections.
Tightening the expanded bbox needs a proof and robust outward rounding; simply deleting the one-cell guard is not accepted.
Nearest-point and projected-area algorithm simplification requires preserving zero-area rejection, within-cell minimum and stable depth/ID ties.

geometry.batch_geometry_policy: one VBO; world meshes and local spheres; independent of B
geometry.input_pose: float32 CUDA B44; row-major camera FLU to world
geometry.output: owned CUDA distance float32 and identity int64 BHW
geometry.output_transfer: whole array to PBO in GL; one CUDA D2D PBO-to-Torch copy
geometry.interop_synchronization: CUDA GL-resource map/unmap on current PyTorch stream
geometry.near_clip_policy: unchanged GL w=forward, clip z=0, no positive near plane
geometry.zone_sampling: exact triangle/cell cone clip and nearest point; no supersampling

measurement_notes: Native hot baseline calls unchanged BatchRenderer.render without hooks.
Isolated stages explicitly finish GL or synchronize CUDA at each boundary; their times must not be added to reconstruct native scheduling.
CPU submit measures API enqueue/host wait time. A CUDA interop map can block.
GL elapsed queries measure GPU command spans; host-only draw state need not have meaningful GPU cost. Query collection is outside recorded stage times.
CUDA events around tiny operations can include host enqueue gaps; copy event duration is not a pure device memcpy bandwidth benchmark.
Pipeline statistics are collected in a separate untimed native render; no statistics query overlaps timed draw measurements.
Pose construction/mounts, scene preparation, shader compilation, sensor postprocessing and validation downloads are outside this profile.
No sampling, geometry, precision, occlusion, output or resolution change.

metadata.name: single_cell_tight_gs
metadata.description: Keep original FP64 full-view GS clip and original FS; emit one cell only when the original triangle is certified strictly inside that cell cone.
caveats: All original vertices must be forward, project into the same legal cell, and be strictly inside all four cone sides.
Each side requires dot > 1e-10 * L1(plane) * max(1, max_abs(vertex)); uncertain/boundary cases use the original expanded rectangle.
A triangle is convex; strict vertex containment proves no positive-area overlap with another cell, in exact arithmetic.
The margin is an engineering guard, not a formal bound on every GPU compiler transformation; validate boundary cases and full-output parity.
No geometry, arithmetic precision, primitive order, fragment coverage test, nearest hit or depth/ID tie rule is changed.

metadata.name: range_aabb_gs
metadata.description: Conservatively reject triangles whose AABB is strictly outside the maximum-range sphere; original FS.
caveats: A triangle is contained in its sensor-space AABB; distance to that AABB is a lower bound on distance to every triangle point.
Reject only lower_sq > max_range_sq + 1e-10 * max(1, lower_sq, max_range_sq); boundary cases fall through.
Only maximum range is used; minimum-range occluders are not removed.
FP64 margin guards ordinary rounding but is not a formal GPU-compiler error bound; validate exact outputs and range-boundary cases.
No mesh, transform, primitive order, surviving fragment algorithm, nearest hit or depth/ID tie rule is changed.
